profile.subseg: BLDC fans; TPW fans; ventilating fans; electric heaters; electric kettles

bull_bear.body: Primarily internal accruals for capex and working capital; modest bank term loans used; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on reinvestment for capacity and product diversification.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: High seasonality of fan demand; reliance on B2B customer relationships (no direct branding); potential margin pressure if BLDC growth slows; MSME payment compliance pressures on working capital; new product lines (heaters/kettles) unproven at scale.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, experienced, and pragmatic; emphasis on delivery reliability, quality, and operational efficiency; avoids overpromising on new products; highlights long-term vendor relationships and lack of listed competition as key advantages.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The company's 'stickiness' with customers is unusually high — nearly all customers have stayed for decades, with attrition only when customers started their own units; this suggests deep operational trust, not just price-based loyalty.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: BLDC fans: 2.35 lakh units in H1FY25 (up from 60k in H1FY24, +291.6%); total units sold: 32.95 lakh in H1FY25; heaters/kettles: new product line, first-year, no revenue share disclosed; TPW fans: growing segment; ventilating fans: core offering.

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin improved to 2.68% in H1FY25; BLDC fans have slightly better margins than induction fans; overall margin improvement driven by volume leverage, cost optimization, and product mix shift, not solely BLDC.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: H1 FY25 revenue was INR361cr (+101% YoY); company aims to maintain similar growth for full FY25; no formal full-year guidance given but management expressed confidence in sustaining momentum.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Fully booked during peak season; idle capacity exists in off-season, partially offset by heaters/kettles production.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into TPW (table, pedestal, wall) plastic fan manufacturing via new INR3cr plant (to commission early FY26); potential to scale heaters/kettles into a material segment over 2-3 years; possible export entry in future.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Wonder Electricals is scaling as India's leading listed fan OEM/ODM, leveraging BLDC growth and off-season appliance diversification to drive 100%+ revenue growth and margin expansion, while strategically expanding capacity via internal accruals. The company's operational discipline, vendor stickiness, and lack of listed peers create a durable competitive moat.
